$comment: JSON Schema for one corpus entry. Written as a schema because that is the form a contributor and a reviewer both already read — but NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY VALIDATES IT WITH A JSON SCHEMA LIBRARY. `jsonschema` is not in tests/requirements-dev.txt, and adding a dependency so that two files agree about a shape is a poor trade; `tests/test_corpus.py` carries a small structural validator that enforces exactly the constraints written here, and a test asserts the two lists of required keys are the same, so the document below cannot drift away from what is actually checked.
title: brAIn corpus entry

schema.description: The entry format. The same number panel/capture.py writes.

kind.description: A `checks` entry carries a house snapshot and the check ids that should fire on it, and is replayed with no model at all — that half runs in ordinary CI and is what fails when a floor moves. An `analyst` entry carries the bundle a real run was given and the reply it produced, and needs a real model to replay. A `first_look` entry carries one batch of signals the Resident's cheap first look judged, the inputs its prompt was built from, and per-signal labels saying the least (`floor`) or most (`ceiling`) a verdict may be: it is replayed against the current prompt, and its guard labels are checked free in CI against an adversary that answers `ignore` for everything.

id.description: Unique within the corpus. For a captured run this is the run id, which is Claude Code's own session id for it.

title.description: One line a person reads in a report.

note.description: Why this entry is in the corpus, and what it is meant to catch.

captured_at.description: Epoch seconds. Never used for grading — every timestamp inside a snapshot is relative to the snapshot's own `now`, which is stored with it, so a replay a year from today grades exactly what a replay today does.

source.description: Which face ran it: card, ask, or fixture for the two built by construction.

snapshot.description: REQUIRED for kind=checks: the house, in the shape checks.snapshot.collect produces. `now` is the instant everything inside it is relative to; `available` says which keys were fetched, and a check whose key is missing is skipped rather than silent.

bundle.description: REQUIRED for kind=analyst: what the analyst was sent. The orientation map for a search run, the slimmed entity bundle for a snapshot one — `gather_mode` says which.

model.description: What answered when this was captured. Recorded, never replayed with: a replay names its own model, because the point is to compare.

reply.description: The parsed card. Never the rendered `html` — that is a picture of up to 200 KB, and what a corpus scores is the findings.

batch.description: REQUIRED for kind=first_look: the signals as `signals.make` produces them, in the order the look numbered them. A label's `signal` is a 1-based index into this list.

now.description: REQUIRED for kind=first_look: the instant every age in the batch is rendered against, so a replay renders the batch exactly as the look saw it.

inputs.description: What a first look's prompt was built from besides the batch — memory, open cases, the clock line, watch notes, worked examples — so a replay rebuilds it with the current builder rather than replaying this release's text.

labels.description: The ground truth. Empty is a real answer for a checks entry — it means every check must be silent on this house — and is never a real answer for an analyst entry, which is unscoreable without one.

oneOf.$comment: A checks label: this check must fire, about this thing.

entity_id.description: What the row has to be about. Omitted means any row from that check counts.

oneOf.$comment: An analyst label: somebody ended this finding, and which button they pressed is what it means. done/got_it/accepted = the report was right (accepted being 'real work, on my to-do list'); wrong = it was not, and reporting it again is a false positive rather than a miss.

finding_key.description: findings_store.normalize of the finding's text, as it was when the ending was given.

note.description: The homeowner's own words, redacted like everything else in the entry.

oneOf.$comment: A first_look label: the least (`floor`) or most (`ceiling`) this signal's verdict could be and still agree with what was true. `guard: true` marks a floor the code enforces after any reply (`resident.never_ignore`), which the free replay checks against an adversary answering `ignore` for everything.

outcome.description: What the household did, for a label the nightly outcomes join derived.
